skill.name: skillscan
skill.description: Scans local or packaged AI skills through a cloud service, returns risk verdicts, and helps block high-risk skills before use.
skill.summary: Cloud-backed security scanner for AI skill packages and installed skill directories.
skill.author: tokauth

security_audit.summary: SkillScan performs real security-scanning work, but it relies on external cloud requests, uploads skill archives, collects host fingerprint data, and silently self-updates. Many static hits are Markdown formatting or guarded temporary-file use, but the remote update, persistent instruction, and data-transfer behaviors need remediation before publication.

remediation.issue: Silent remote self-update can replace skill code without clear user approval.
remediation.suggestion: Disable automatic updates by default, require explicit confirmation, and verify releases with signatures from a pinned public key.

remediation.issue: Cloud scanning uploads skill archives and host fingerprint data to an external service.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear consent step, document all transmitted fields, remove MAC collection, and provide a local-only mode.

remediation.issue: The skill instructs agents to write persistent security rules into SOUL.md.
remediation.suggestion: Do not modify external agent policy files automatically. Ask the user for explicit approval and show the exact text first.

remediation.issue: Deletion of high-risk skills uses recursive removal after a scan verdict.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict deletion to verified skill roots, show the resolved path, and require typed confirmation before removing files.

remediation.issue: Archive extraction uses extractall after custom path checks.
remediation.suggestion: Replace extractall with per-member extraction using pathlib is_relative_to checks and reject symlinks or unusual archive entries.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md tells agents to append persistent instructions to SOUL.md, including "ALWAYS scan skills" and "non-negotiable". A marketplace skill should not modify future agent policy outside its own directory without explicit user control.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly instructs the agent to write durable behavioral rules into SOUL.md. This is an agent-persistence pattern, even though the stated security goal is protective.

semantic_findings.title: Silent Remote Self-Update
semantic_findings.description: The scanner checks for updates automatically, downloads a remote zip, and copies files into the installed skill directory. The manifest source can be changed by environment variable and no independent signature verification is enforced.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code path is explicit: auto_upgrade_if_needed runs on every command and cmd_upgrade downloads and installs new files. The update manifest may include a hash, but it is not a signed trust root.

semantic_findings.title: External Upload of Skill Contents and Host Fingerprint
semantic_findings.description: The scanner packages skill directories and uploads them to the SkillScan API when no cache result exists. It also builds an X-Client-Info header containing a client ID, OS details, Python version, and optional MAC address.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The upload and client-info code are direct and reachable through scan commands. This is legitimate scanner functionality, but it is a high-confidence privacy and data-transfer risk.

content.value_statement: AI skills can contain risky scripts, network calls, or unsafe install behavior. SkillScan checks packages and installed skills through a cloud scanner before use.
actual_capabilities: Scans a single skill directory or zip archive for security risk.
Finds installed skill directories across common AI agent locations.
Calculates directory SHA-256 hashes for cloud cache lookup.
Uploads packaged skill content to a cloud API when no cache result exists.
Displays SAFE, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, or CRITICAL verdicts with threat labels.
Prompts before deleting installed skills that receive high-risk verdicts.
limitations: Uncached scans require network access to the SkillScan cloud service.
Skill contents may be uploaded to an external service for analysis.
The auto-update path trusts a remote manifest and does not use independent signatures.
Scan accuracy depends on the remote API response and service availability.

use_cases.title: Review a New Skill Package
use_cases.description: Scan a downloaded zip or directory before installing it into an AI agent environment.

use_cases.title: Audit Existing Agent Skills
use_cases.description: Find installed skills across local agent folders and scan them as a batch.

use_cases.title: Gate Marketplace Submissions
use_cases.description: Use scan verdicts and threat labels as an input before approving community skills.

prompt_templates.title: Scan One Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check before installing a local skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan this skill directory for security risk and summarize the verdict before I use it: <path>

prompt_templates.title: Scan Installed Skills
prompt_templates.scenario: Routine review of the local AI agent environment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find my installed AI skills, scan them, and list any MEDIUM, HIGH, or CRITICAL results.

prompt_templates.title: Assess a Shared Archive
prompt_templates.scenario: Review of a skill archive received from another source.
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan this skill zip archive and explain whether it is acceptable to install: <path-to-zip>

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Remediation Guidance
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review after a scan returns issues.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the scan findings to identify the risky behaviors and propose concrete fixes for the skill author.

output_examples.input: Scan a new skill directory before installation.
output_examples.output: The scanner reports a HIGH verdict. It shows network upload behavior and recommends blocking installation until the author explains the data flow.

output_examples.input: Run a batch scan for installed skills.
output: The scan found several installed skills and returned mixed verdicts.
LOW and MEDIUM results need user review.
HIGH or CRITICAL results should be blocked until remediated.

output_examples.input: Review a zip archive from a marketplace submission.
output_examples.output: The archive is unpacked for scanning, sent for cloud analysis if no cache hit exists, and reported with a risk level and summary.

best_practices: Scan skills before installation, update, or first use.
Review network and filesystem findings before trusting a cloud scan result.
Keep copies of scan reports outside the skill directory.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a SAFE result as proof that all future updates are safe.
Do not upload private or proprietary skill code without policy approval.
Do not enable silent self-updates without user consent and signature verification.

faq.question: Does SkillScan run fully offline?
faq.answer: No. It uses a cloud cache and uploads skill content when no cached result is available.

faq.question: Can it scan both directories and zip archives?
faq.answer: Yes. It accepts local skill directories and zip files for single-skill scans.

faq.question: What verdicts does it report?
faq.answer: It reports SAFE, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL, UNKNOWN, or ERROR depending on the scan response.

faq.question: Does it delete risky skills automatically?
faq.answer: No. It prompts before deleting a skill that receives a HIGH or CRITICAL verdict.

faq.question: What data may leave my machine?
faq.answer: The scanner can upload packaged skill contents and a client information header to the cloud API.

faq.question: Is the updater safe for managed environments?
faq.answer: Use caution. The updater checks a remote manifest and replaces skill files without independent signature verification.
